original.description: German infantry crowd the open door of a goods wagon of the Reichseisenbahnen in Elsass-Lothringen (marked 'Elsaß-Lothringen 33644 Gm'), waving, raising fists, holding flowers and a letter; the wagon is chalked 'Ausflug nach Paris — Auf Wiedersehn auf dem Boulevard' and 'Auf in den Kampf, mir juckt die Säbelspitze'; two men in shirtsleeves lean from the side hatch; oak sprigs on the door. August 1914, en route to the front.
inscriptions: Auf in den Kampf, mir juckt die Säbelspitze

caption: 'Excursion to Paris — see you on the Boulevard.' German infantry in a goods wagon of the Alsace-Lorraine railways, August 1914: the mobilization timetable in human form, and the confidence that it would all be over in six weeks. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: anonymous, August 1914, via greatwar.nl and Wikimedia Commons; public domain. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-22. Candidate hero for the opening sequence and the railways tech card — the chalked 'Ausflug nach Paris' is the thesis ('a timetable the world fell behind') stated by the men themselves. The wagon's Alsace-Lorraine marking ties it to the annexed provinces and the 1870 prequel. The print is widely reproduced; trace the holding archive (German federal or state photo collections) for the pipeline.
